newsitem.title: USA: Fidelity Magellan raised stock holdings in February.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity Magellan raised stock holdings in February.

text.p: Fidelity Investments' flagship Magellan Fund raised its stock holdings at the end of February and cut its holdings in cash and bonds, according to the monthly Fidelity Mutual Fund Guide released Wednesday.
The nation's largest mutual fund company also said it had a negative return of 0.56 percent for the first three months this year.

The Boston-based investment firm said it raised its stock holdings to 95.5 percent of assets in February -- the most recent month for which figures are available -- from 93.5 percent at the end of January.
At the same time, it cut its holdings in bonds to zero at the end of February from 0.8 percent a month earlier.
Magellan also lowered its holdings in cash to 4.5 percent of assets from 5.7 percent.
The fund said it had a negative return of 0.56 percent from January through March this year, underperforming the 2.68 percent gain for the Standard & Poor's 500 Composite index over the same period.

Since he took over Magellan in June, fund manager Robert Stansky has gradually shifted the fund into stocks and out of its massive investment in bonds, which hurt the funds returns over the past year when the stock market recorded strong gains.
Total assets in the massive fund fell to $51.4 billion at the end of March from $53.8 billion at the end of February, Fidelity said.

The company said it trimmed its holdings in technology stocks to 13.8 percent from 14.6 percent, cut energy shares to 13.1 percent from 14.6 percent, and raised its holding of financial stocks to 10.5 percent from 9.6 percent.
Assets in durables slipped to 8.8 percent from 8.9 percent, industrial machinery and equipment rose to 7.9 percent from 7.7 percent, and healthcare shares rose to 7.3 percent from 6.3 percent.
Magellan said it added Merck & Co. Inc, Exxon Corp. and American International Group Inc. to its top 10 holdings at the end of February.
The fund cut International Business Machines Corp., Royal Dutch Petroleum Co. and Cisco Systems Inc. from its top 10 holdings, Fidelity said.
Remaining among the top 10 were General Electric Co., Intel Corp., Philip Morris Cos. Inc., CSX Corp., Chrysler Corp., Citicorp and Schlumberger Ltd.
Investments in foreign securities slipped to 9.9 percent of assets at the end of February from 10.4 percent at the end of January.
